newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to meet Chirac next month.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to meet Chirac next month.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin is due to meet French President Jacques Chirac near Moscow on February 2 and Russia's relations with NATO will be high on the agenda, the Kremlin said on Monday.
Presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzembsky said the meeting would take place at a country residence near Moscow.
It forms part of a busy international schedule for Yeltsin, who returned to work last month after undergoing heart surgery on November 5.
Yeltsin met German Chancellor Helmut Kohl at his residence on Saturday and is expected to hold talks with British Prime Minister John Major soon.
Yeltsin has also accepted an invitation to Germany in April and will have talks in The Hague on February 4 with the current European Union president, Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok.
He will travel to the United States in March for talks with President Bill Clinton and again in June for the Group of Seven major industrial nations' summit in Denver.

Yastrzembsky said Yeltsin's meeting with Kohl had brought little progress on Russia's relations with NATO, which is expected to invite some former East bloc countries this year to join, despite Moscow's fierce opposition.
Yastrzhembsky said it had become clear that the issue would dominate the international agenda this year.

"The question of Russia-NATO in its broadest context is issue number one in international relations this year and the coming contacts and meetings involving the Russian president will undoubtedly touch on this issue in one way or another," he said.
